newsitem.title: USA: US junk corp bond deals crowd end-of-week calendar.
newsitem.headline: US junk corp bond deals crowd end-of-week calendar.

text.p: Nine new high-yield corporate bond issues, representing over $1.5 billion in new supply, are expected to hit the market on Thursday and Friday, syndicate officials said.
High-yield bond investors, their coffers filled with new cash, are likely to easily absorb the new paper, they added.
Investment-grade bond issuance is expected to take a breather following yesterday's massive $4.3 billion debt offering by Norfolk Southern Corp, syndicate officials said.
One exception may be CIGNA Corp, which is readying a $600 million offering of 10-year and 30-year bonds.
Goldman Sachs & Co is the underwriter of the deal.

In the high-yield market, Coleman Escrow Corp, a holding company of Coleman Co Inc, is expected to issue $470 million in four-year zero coupon bonds in a 144a private placement via Bear Stearns & Co Inc on Thursday.
Coleman, a camping supply company owned by financier Ronald Perlman, will use the proceeds to refinance outstanding zero coupon bonds and convertible notes issued by other Coleman holding companies.
The new bonds will be collateralized by 44.1 million shares of common stock of Coleman owned by Perlman.
The offering will consist of $390 million in first priority senior secured discount notes and $80 million in second priority senior secured discount notes.
Price talk on the first priority notes is 11 percent to 11.125 percent. Talk on the second priority notes is 175 basis points to 200 basis points over the first priority notes.
Williams Scotsman Inc is also readying a $400 million 144a offering of 10-year senior notes via BT Securities Corp.
The company, which is in the mobile office unit leasing business, will use the proceeds to refinance outstanding debt.
Price talk on the B3-rated deal is in the 10 percent area.

Expected for Friday is AFC Enterprises Inc's $175 million offering of 10-year senior subordinated notes, Pogo Producing Co's $100 million 10-year senior subordinated note deal, Windy Hill Pet Food Co's offering of $100 million 10-year senior subordinated note, Profitt's Inc's $100 million senior note deal and Wiser Oil Co's $100 million 10-year senior subordinated note offering.
All the offerings are 144a private placements, syndicate sources said.
-Douglas Brown, 212-859-1662
Also for Thursday, Von Hoffmann Press Inc plans to sell $75 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp.
Proceeds from the 144a private placement will be used to finance a leveraged buyout of the company by a DLJ investment partnership and the company's management.
Von Hoffmann manufactures textbooks for major educational publishers such as Harcourt Brace & Co and Houghton Mifflin Co.
Price talk on the deal, which is rated B3/B minus, is in the 10 3/8 percent area, syndicate officials said.
